# has

> Test if a [JSON Pointer][json-pointer] ([RFC 6901][rfc-6901]) resolves to a value in a document.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var has = require( '@stdlib/utils/json-pointer/has' );
```

#### has( document, pointer )

Tests if a [JSON Pointer][json-pointer] resolves to a value in a document.

```javascript
var obj = {
    'foo': [ 'bar', 'baz' ]
};
var bool = has( obj, '/foo/0' );
// returns true

obj = {
    'foo': 'bar'
};
bool = has( obj, '/foo' );
// returns true

bool = has( obj, '/missing' );
// returns false

bool = has( obj, '' );
// returns true
```

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   Per [RFC 6901][rfc-6901], an empty string refers to the root of the document and returns `true` for any valid object or array.
-   The `-` token on an array references the position after the last element (nonexistent element), so it returns `false`.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

## Examples

```javascript
var has = require( '@stdlib/utils/json-pointer/has' );

var doc = {
    'foo': [ 'bar', 'baz' ],
    '': 0,
    'a/b': 1,
    'm~n': 8
};

var bool = has( doc, '/foo' );
// returns true

bool = has( doc, '/foo/0' );
// returns true

bool = has( doc, '/foo/99' );
// returns false

bool = has( doc, '/foo/-' );
// returns false

bool = has( doc, '/' );
// returns true

bool = has( doc, '/a~1b' );
// returns true

bool = has( doc, '/m~0n' );
// returns true

bool = has( doc, '/nonexistent' );
// returns false

bool = has( doc, '' );
// returns true
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->
